title: Triangular minimal-polynomial data and independent bounded products
statement: For fields k and K with a k-algebra structure, a finite transcendence basis x:Fin d→K and a finite family b:Fin m→K, there exist nonzero h in k[X], monic triangular polynomials p_i, variable assignments y and degrees e_i equal to natDegree p_i. The assignments y are x, inverse h(x), and b. Every triangularFieldModelEquations polynomial evaluates to zero at y. The products of b_i with exponents indexed by functions a:(i:Fin m)→Fin(e_i) are linearly independent over the intermediate field k(x). This asserts no kernel equality or coordinate map.

source.place: Proof of Tag 07BV, first assertion, triangular minimal polynomials and denominator clearing; Tag 08JZ, localization presentation. Read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07BV and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08JZ because the local literature checkout is absent.

proof.text: Set F=k(x). The transcendence-basis hypothesis gives Algebra.IsAlgebraic F K, hence all b_i are integral over F. Apply exists_algebraicTower_triangularRelations to obtain monic q_i over F in preceding variables, their vanishing, and independent bounded products.

source.place: Proof of Tag 07BV, first assertion: inductive monic polynomial relations over the rational function field; field tower ingredients in Tags 09G1, 09GN and 09G9.

proof.text: Apply exists_triangularRelations_denominatorLift to q_i and algebraic independence of x. Obtain h nonzero and monic p_i of unchanged degrees, with their coefficient evaluation identities. Use e_i=natDegree(q_i), so the independent product family is unchanged.

source.place: Proof of Tag 07BV, first assertion: choosing one h for all polynomial coefficients; Tag 08JZ, localization variable evaluating to inverse h.

proof.text: Define y explicitly by testing whether its index is less than d, equal to d, or greater than d: use x, inverse h(x), and the appropriately shifted b, respectively. Algebraic independence gives h(x) nonzero, so the localization equation evaluates to h(x)h(x) inverse minus 1=0. For each remaining list equation, restrict y to the coefficient variables, use the coefficient map equality, and apply Polynomial.hom_eval₂ and eval_map to its original vanishing q_i(b_i)=0. Return the constructed data and its independent products.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_triangularFieldModel_data
    (k : Type u) (K : Type v) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (d : ℕ) (x : Fin d → K) (hx : IsTranscendenceBasis k x)
    (m : ℕ) (b : Fin m → K) :
    ∃ (h : MvPolynomial (Fin d) k)
      (p : (i : Fin m) → Polynomial (MvPolynomial (Fin (d + 1 + i.val)) k))
      (y : Fin (d + 1 + m) → K) (e : Fin m → ℕ),
      h ≠ 0 ∧ (∀ i, (p i).Monic) ∧ (∀ i, (p i).natDegree = e i) ∧
      (∀ j : Fin d, y ⟨j.val, by omega⟩ = x j) ∧
      y ⟨d, by omega⟩ = (MvPolynomial.aeval x h)⁻¹ ∧
      (∀ i : Fin m, y ⟨d + 1 + i.val, by omega⟩ = b i) ∧
      (∀ q ∈ triangularFieldModelEquations k d m h p, MvPolynomial.aeval y q = 0) ∧
      LinearIndependent (IntermediateField.adjoin k (Set.range x))
        (fun a : ((i : Fin m) → Fin (e i)) => ∏ i, b i ^ (a i).val)
